title: APAC Latency-Price Arbitrage Radar for Edge Model Procurement
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: build a reproducible radar and trigger matrix that recommends when to procure or switch to alternative model variants for APAC edge deployments based on observed latency tails, token-unit economics, and capacity availability.

Scope: evaluate 6 candidate model variants (float16, int8/quantized, small/large) across 3 edge regions (JP, SG, AU) with representative production prompt mixes. Deliverables: (1) Radar dashboard with P50/P95 latency vs 1k-token cost per model/region; (2) Procurement trigger matrix that maps observed metrics to actionable ops steps (reserve, burst to hosted, switch variant, circuit-break); (3) Runbook for SRE/Platform with rollback and measurement instrumentation.

Motivation: APAC customers report sensitive UX degradation at P95 > 80ms for search snippets; procurement decisions must consider both unit cost and capacity lead time (reserved capacity procurement lead times vary by partner). This ticket operationalizes an arbitrage signal (latency delta vs price delta) to reduce false-positive procurements while catching real capacity/latency risks.
acceptance_criteria: Radar dashboard updateable from nightly ingest
Trigger matrix contains concrete numeric thresholds for P50/P95 and cost deltas
Runbook includes escalation flow and git-tagged automation scripts in repo
SLO delta test demonstrating <10% user-visible error when switching variants

notes: Initial thresholds proposed: P95 trigger JP=85ms SG=90ms AU=95ms; cost-arbitrage trigger: switch to dedicated if price per 1k tokens for hosted exceeds dedicated amortized cost by >35% and observed P95 degradation >10%
Quantization trade-off: int8 reduces tail by ~8% in lab vs fp16 but may increase hallucination on long-chain prompts—research to add eval set for hallucination rate required before auto-switching
SRE guidance: any automatic procurement action requires two checkpoints: (1) metric convergence over 3 daily windows, (2) an automated canary (5% traffic) with human approval for full rollout
